nodes.name: MOF Precursor Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The NiFeCoCuMo metal-organic framework (MOF) precursors with 2,5-dihydroxyterephthalic acid as the organic ligand were synthesized.
nodes.source_text: First, the NiFeCoCuMo metal-organic framework (MOF) precursors with 2,5-dihydroxyterephthalic acid as the organic ligand were synthesized (Figures S1 and S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Flash Joule Heating Pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: The high-entropy MOF structure not only facilitates the high dispersion of metal atoms but also enables its organic ligand to serve as a carbon source for the reduction of metal atoms during pyrolysis. The MOF precursors were then pyrolyzed by the Joule-heating approach for just 30s at 800°C (Figure S3, Supporting Information), followed by rapid cooling to lock the final HEA-Mo2C heterostructure in place. Notably, the carburization reaction of Mo plays a central role in the formation of biphasic Janus structures. Within an extremely short heating time (≤1s), the carburization process of Mo is kinetically inhibited, resulting in a high-entropy alloy (HEA) composed of Ni, Fe, Co, Cu, and Mo. When the heating time is increased (10s), the XRD spectrum shows the characteristic peak of MoC. As the heating time increases (20-40s), the characteristic peak of Mo2C gradually appears, confirming the conversion of MoC to Mo2C.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1.0 M KOH + seawater (three-electrode)
nodes.source_text: The prepared catalysts were then evaluated for electrocatalytic OER activities in alkaline seawater with real-time iR correction. The linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) curves display that the HEA Mo₂C only requires an overpotential of 296 mV to deliver the current density of 100 mA cm⁻²... HEA-Mo₂C displays low overpotentials of 333 mV at 500 mA cm⁻²... Tafel slope for HEA-Mo₂C is 35 mV dec⁻¹... mass current density (385.89 A g⁻¹) and specific activity (1.53 mA cm⁻²)... corrosion potential (E_corr, 0.81 V)... Faradaic efficiency of ≈100%... remained unchanged after 50 h... stability for over 250 h

nodes.description: AEMWE overall water splitting performance (HEA-Mo₂C || Pt/C)
nodes.source_text: When deployed in anion-exchange membrane electrolyzers, the heterostructured catalyst achieves industrial-grade current density (1 A cm⁻² at 1.96 V) with excellent stability over 1000 h at 500 mA cm⁻²... AEMWE using HEA-Mo₂C as the OER catalyst... requires only a voltage of 1.96 V... function steadily for over 1000 h, with the voltage increasing by only 0.096 V... kinetic overpotential and mass-transport overpotential... 399 and 107 mV at 1 A cm⁻²

nodes.description: AEMWE stability in 1 M KOH + 2.5 M NaCl at 60°C
nodes.source_text: we tested the stability of the electrolyzer under severe operating conditions (1 M KOH + 2.5 M NaCl, 60°C). The catalyst is stable at 500 mA cm⁻² for 130 h with almost no degradation, and its Faradaic efficiency for O₂ production is maintained at a high level (94%)

nodes.description: OER stability in 1.0 M KOH + seawater (chronoamperometry)
nodes.source_text: the Faradaic efficiency for OER of the catalyst remained unchanged after 50 h of continuous working at 100 mA cm⁻²

nodes.description: OER stability test with added 0.05 M MoO₄²⁻
nodes.source_text: we tested the stability of NiFeCoCu in alkaline seawater electrolyte with 0.05 M MoO₄²⁻. However, the OER stability of NiFeCoCu is not enhanced in the new electrolyte

nodes.characterization_summary: HEA-Mo2C shows characteristic peaks of Mo2C (PDF# 79-0744) and HEA (111) phases with XRD peak intensity ratio of Mo2C (121) to HEA (111) increasing with heating time.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Additionally, the XRD peak intensity ratio of Mo2C (121) to HEA (111) increases with longer heating times, which indicates an increased content of Mo2C.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals lattice spacings of 0.254 nm for Mo2C (002) planes and 0.186 nm for HEA (100) planes in the Janus particles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic phase images further reveal more details about the HEA and Mo2C phases in these Janus particles; the measured lattice spacings of 0.254 and 0.186 nm can be attributed to the (002) planes of Mo2C and (100) planes of HEA, respectively (Figure 1e–g).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM exhibits clear phase boundary and two distinct phase structures with symmetrical distribution of molybdenum carbide and high-entropy alloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) for the HEA-Mo2C exhibits a clear phase boundary and two distinct phase structures, indicating that the structure of HEA-Mo2C consists of a symmetrical distribution of molybdenum carbide and high-entropy alloy (Figure 1b-d; Figure S11, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic-resolution EDX mappings show Ni, Fe, Co, Cu homogeneously distributed in HEA part and more Mo in Mo2C part, confirming Janus heterojunction structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic-resolution energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) mappings of the heterojunction interface indicate that Ni, Fe, Co, Cu, and a small amount of Mo are homogeneously distributed at the HEA part, while more Mo species stay at the Mo2C part, which confirms the Janus heterojunction structures of one particle composited by half HEA and half Mo2C (Figure 1h,i).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES determines weight ratio of Mo (23.9 wt%), Ni (30.5 wt%), Fe (14.3 wt%), Co (5.04 wt%), Cu (5.47 wt%) in HEA-Mo2C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Furthermore, the weight ratio of Mo, Ni, Fe, Co, and Cu species in HEA-Mo2C is determined to be 23.9, 30.5, 14.3, 5.04, and 5.47 wt.% by inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) (Figure S12, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during OER shows M-O peaks shifting to M-OOH indicating reconstruction to active MOOH species at lower potential for HEA-Mo2C vs NiFeCoCu; time-dependent spectra show MoOx (815 cm⁻¹) formation then conversion to MoO₄²⁻ (905 cm⁻¹) after 40 min.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the process of increasing the applied potentials, the Raman peaks at 310 cm⁻¹ (Fe-O), 470/565 cm⁻¹ (M-O), and 670 cm⁻¹ (Co-O) shifted to 472/553 cm⁻¹ (M-OOH) for HEA-Mo₂C, HEA, and NiFeCoCu... Importantly, the structural transformation of HEA-Mo₂C and HEA occurs at a lower potential compared to NiFeCoCu... The Raman peak at 815 cm⁻¹ assigned to MoOₓ is formed... eventually disappearing completely after 40 min. Meanwhile, the signal of MoO₄²⁻ at 905 cm⁻¹ appears...

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-250h OER TEM shows Mo2C phase mostly dissolved, forming core-shell nanoparticles with 3-6 nm amorphous shell and crystalline HEA core with 0.202 nm (111) lattice spacing.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3c shows that the Mo2C phase of the catalyst is mostly dissolved after OER for 250 h, and the reconstructed HEA-Mo2C nanoparticles exhibit a core-shell structure with a 3-6 nm amorphous shell while the core still preserves a highly crystalline structure (Figure 3d). The HR-TEM image shows a lattice spacing of 0.202 nm according to the (111) facet of HEA...

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER XPS shows reduced M0 signals for Ni, Fe; Mo 3d shifts to Mo6+ peaks at 233.7 and 236.8 eV confirming Mo2C oxidation to MoO4^2-.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared to HEA-Mo2C before OER, the intensity of M0 (M = Ni, Fe, Co, Cu) signals was significantly reduced... the Mo 3d peak of the HEA-Mo2C before OER can be deconvoluted to binding energies of Mo0 (228.3 and 231.6 eV), Mo2+ (228.9 and 232.2 eV), and Mo4+ (233.2 and 235.4 eV). After long-term OER test, the Mo 3d spectrum exhibits the main doublet peaks at 233.7 and 236.8 eV (Mo6+ 3d5/2 and Mo6+ 3d3/2)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER Ni K-edge XANES shows absorption edge between Ni foil and NiO (closer to Ni⁰); Mo K-edge shows average valence between Mo⁴⁺ and Mo⁶⁺ confirming surface MoO₄²⁻ formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra at Ni K-edge exhibit a slightly higher absorption edge position than that of Ni foil and much lower than that of NiO, suggesting an average valence between Ni⁰ to Ni²⁺ and much closer to Ni⁰... Moreover, the XANES of HEA-Mo₂C after OER at the Mo K-edge shows an average oxidation valence state of Mo atoms between Mo⁴⁺ and Mo⁶⁺...

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS at Ni K-edge shows Ni-O at 1.76 Å and Ni-Ni at 2.27 Å; Mo K-edge shows predominant Mo-O at 1.33 Å and weak Mo-Mo at 2.71 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier-transformed (FT) of k3-weighted extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra at Ni K-edge show a weak peak at 1.76 Å and a predominant peak at 2.27 Å, which can be attributed to Ni-O and Ni-Ni bond... The FT curves of the Mo K-edge data display a predominant Mo-O coordination (1.33 Å) and weak Mo-Mo coordination (2.71 Å)...

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ FT-IR shows *OOH peak at 1108 cm-1 increasing with potential and higher O-H stretching bands (3200-3600 cm-1) indicating more *OH adsorption on HEA-Mo2C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Figure 4a,b, the peak at 1108 cm-1 attributed to the key intermediate of OER (*OOH) increases with the increase of working potential. Additionally, the bands from 3200 to 3600 cm-1 assigned to the O-H stretching mode (νO-H) of *OH are higher on the HEA-Mo2C catalyst than the NiFeCoCu...
